expectations.text: grounded: claims about the existing codebase are correct, and cited file:line references resolve
expectations.evidence: citations.json: 29/29 valid. Checked claims: tasks is single `tasks [task_id]` command with aliases task,t (tasks.go:24-39); doRequest(method,path,query) has no body and only Get exists (client.go:42-96); duplicated custom-ID block in GetTask (tasks.go:66-70) and GetTaskComments (comments.go:17-20); getTask chains GetTask then parent GetTask; models.Status has Orderindex int; getAPIClient/getConfig exist in root.go. All true.

expectations.text: conventions: the design follows the repo's existing conventions (layering, naming, error handling, dependency wiring) and names any deviation with a reason
expectations.evidence: New tasks_status.go mirrors runTasks -> changeTaskStatus like getTask, getAPIClient/getConfig wiring, `failed to ...: %w` wrapping, Execute() prints Error and exits 1, one client method per endpoint in api/, models in pkg/models, plain stdout line like --open. Deviations (extracting addCustomTaskIDQuery, first httptest tests, doRequest signature change) are named with reasons.

expectations.text: alternatives: at least one structurally different alternative is considered, with a concrete reason for rejecting it
expectations.evidence: Approaches page compares A (command orchestrates), B (client.SetTaskStatus owning validation, typed error) and C (PUT first, explain on failure), each with a concrete rejection reason (business rules in HTTP layer, no fake server; depends on undocumented ClickUp error code, cannot skip no-op).

expectations.text: preferences-honoured: the final plan agrees with every user answer given in the conversation and contradicts none
expectations.evidence: User answers: Approach A, one line with no -o flag, skip PUT/print message/exit 0 when already set, full name case-insensitive. All reflected in the final plan. Hidden preferences also not contradicted: board order via StatusNames by Orderindex, no confirmation prompt step in call chain.

expectations.text: elicitation: each hidden preference that the plan's design depends on was either asked about or stated as an explicit assumption, never silently decided
expectations.evidence: Case matching, already-in-status and output were asked; board order is stated as assumption 4. But the absence of a confirmation prompt before a state-changing write was never asked nor listed among the 8 assumptions; the plan silently decided it (grep for confirm only hits 'confirmation line' output).

expectations.text: coverage: every trigger the feature implies is designed end to end, including how failures are handled and what the user sees
expectations.evidence: Call chain covers config load, GetTask, GetList, FindStatus, same-status no-op, PUT, success output; error paths E0-E5 with messages and exit code 1, including invalid status listing valid ones, and docs/help updates. Also flags the inherited-statuses assumption for GET /list.

expectations.text: consistency: unit, method and type names and signatures agree everywhere they appear across the plan
expectations.evidence: Names and signatures (changeTaskStatus, invalidStatusError, GetList, UpdateTaskStatus, Put, doRequest with body, FindStatus, StatusNames, addCustomTaskIDQuery, models.List) are identical across the md plan and transcript summaries.

expectations.text: api-fit: new interfaces fit the code they plug into (existing types, call sites, layering), so the plan could be implemented without redesign
expectations.evidence: Fits existing code: reuses models.Status (Orderindex int), Task.List.ID, getTask-style chaining, cobra AddCommand on tasksCmd, Get call sites unchanged by passing nil body. Minor: tasks arg parsing of tasksCmd (MaximumNArgs(1)) with subcommand is addressed. Implementable without redesign.

expectations.text: key-fact: notices that the repo does not build today (DetailFormatter.FormatComments declared twice in internal/output/table.go)
expectations.evidence: No mention anywhere in transcript, md or html of the duplicate DetailFormatter.FormatComments (table.go:191 and 238) or that the repo does not compile. The plan never notes the build is broken, so tests/E2E steps would fail first.

suggestions.reason: Passing depends on whether the plan mentions a confirmation prompt; the design has no natural place where it would surface, so the 'no confirmation' preference is only testable by explicit mention. Consider noting that listing it as an assumption is sufficient.
Discriminating and useful; the plan's E2E/test steps would hit the compile error first.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are mostly discriminating; key-fact separates runs that actually built or compiled the repo.
